What if AI could help humans live to 150?
Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, believes artificial intelligence could accelerate medical research so dramatically that human lifespans might double within the next decade.

His reasoning? AI could accelerate scientific discoveries by 10x, compressing 50–100 years of biological and medical progress into just 5–10 years after the arrival of sufficiently powerful AI. Dario Amodei
And the longevity race is already underway.
Jeff Bezos has backed Altos Labs. Sam Altman has invested in Retro Biosciences. Meanwhile, experimental cellular rejuvenation therapies are entering human clinical trials.

In 2026, Life Biosciences began testing ER-100, an experimental treatment designed to restore cellular function in patients with certain eye diseases. Retro Biosciences has also advanced RTR242, a drug targeting autophagy, the cellular process responsible for recycling damaged components, into human testing. Life Biosciences, Inc.
None of this proves that humans will soon live twice as long. But the scientific possibilities are becoming increasingly interesting.

Here's the real question:
What if the most important thing you can do over the next decade is simply stay healthy enough to benefit from the breakthroughs that might arrive?
The future of longevity isn't guaranteed. But taking care of your health today is already worth the effort.
Explore Longy, your personal AI team for health and longevity.

items.title: 40 AI Agents Built a Superman Flight Simulator in 7 Hours (45M Tokens)
items.excerpt: What happens when you unleash an army of AI coding agents on a single project? Apparently, you get a browser-based Superman flight simulator. Developer vakovalskii built SKYFLY, a surprisingly ambitious 3D flying game wh
items.videoDescription:
What happens when you unleash an army of AI coding agents on a single project?

Apparently, you get a browser-based Superman flight simulator.

Developer vakovalskii built SKYFLY, a surprisingly ambitious 3D flying game where you can soar over Moscow and Saint Petersburg like Superman.

And the development process was almost as insane as the result.

The reported numbers:

- Up to 40 AI agents working simultaneously
- 45 million tokens consumed
- Around 7 hours of development
- Three $100 subscription limits exhausted
- Claude Opus, Astra, DeepSeek, Qwen, and a ridiculous amount of iteration

The result? A playable 3D world running directly in your browser.

You can fly over real-world cities, accelerate to supersonic speeds, explore detailed terrain and buildings, interact with other players, and even punch holes through clouds.

The game uses JavaScript, Three.js, real-world geographic data, and WebSocket multiplayer.

No installation required. Just open your browser and start flying. 

What's more fascinating: this isn't simply AI generating a few lines of code. It's an example of large-scale parallel AI-assisted development, where dozens of coding agents contribute to a single interactive project.

45 million tokens. Seven hours. One flying superhero.

And we're only getting started with agentic coding.

Play SKYFLY:  https://fly.neuraldeep.ru/

GitHub repository:  https://github.com/vakovalskii/skyfly

#AIAgents #ClaudeCode #VibeCoding #FlightSimulator #AgenticCoding

items.title: Claude Code Built a GTA Mod for SimCity 3000 in Just 2 Hours
items.excerpt: What if you could turn almost any PC game into something completely different using AI? And what if Claude Code could handle the modding process for you? Meet Universal Modder, an open-source collection of AI agent skill
items.videoDescription:
What if you could turn almost any PC game into something completely different using AI?
And what if Claude Code could handle the modding process for you?

Meet Universal Modder, an open-source collection of AI agent skills and tools designed to make game modding dramatically easier.
Instead of simply asking Claude to figure out how to modify a game, Universal Modder gives it a structured workflow, technical knowledge, and specialized tools.
And the results can get pretty ridiculous. 

In just a couple of hours, it helped create a GTA-style mod for SimCity 3000.
Yes, that SimCity 3000. The classic city-building game from 1999.
And it didn't stop there. The workflow also produced a promotional video featuring actual gameplay footage from the mod.

What Universal Modder can do:
- Analyze games and identify their engines and modding possibilities
- Research existing modding techniques and reverse-engineer game systems
- Generate custom sprites, textures, 3D models, and audio
- Build and test modifications inside actual games
- Record real gameplay footage
- Create promotional videos showcasing the results
- Reuse accumulated modding knowledge across projects

It supports Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, and other AI coding agents.
The interesting part isn't just that AI can modify old games.

It's that giving AI agents specialized skills and proven workflows can produce much better results than simply asking them to figure everything out from scratch.

A GTA-style mod inside SimCity 3000, complete with its own gameplay trailer, is a pretty entertaining demonstration of that idea.
We're entering an era where modding games might become less about knowing how to code and more about knowing what you want to create.

Universal Modder on GitHub:
https://github.com/rehan-remade/universal-modder
Open source, MIT licensed.

#ClaudeCode #AIGameModding #SimCity3000 #VibeCoding #AIAgents

items.title: Someone Put Claude AI on a 2007 Nokia. Yes, Really.
items.excerpt: Remember when phones had buttons, batteries lasted forever, and Snake was peak entertainment? Well, someone just brought Claude AI to a Nokia from 2007. Developer Emir Karşıyakalı created an open-source AI chat client fo
items.videoDescription:
Remember when phones had buttons, batteries lasted forever, and Snake was peak entertainment?
Well, someone just brought Claude AI to a Nokia from 2007.

Developer Emir Karşıyakalı created an open-source AI chat client for Nokia Series 40 phones, including the legendary Nokia 6300.
And yes, it actually works.

You can type questions on a physical keypad, send them to Claude, and get AI-generated responses on that tiny 240×320 screen.
No touchscreen. No modern smartphone. Just good old Java ME, a small Go server, and some wonderfully unnecessary engineering.

The project has since evolved into AIKON, supporting ChatGPT, Gemini, and Grok alongside Claude.
The AI runs remotely, but the nostalgia is 100% local.
2007 hardware. 2026 intelligence.

GitHub: https://github.com/emir/claude-s40

#ClaudeAI #Nokia #RetroTech #ArtificialIntelligence #Shorts

items.title: Odyssey-3: AI Generates Interactive Worlds in Real Time (And You Can Play Them)
items.excerpt: What if AI could generate an entire world while you're exploring it? Not a video. Not a traditional game. An interactive environment that responds to your actions in real time. Meet Odyssey-3, a new AI world model that g
items.videoDescription:
What if AI could generate an entire world while you're exploring it?
Not a video. Not a traditional game. An interactive environment that responds to your actions in real time.
Meet Odyssey-3, a new AI world model that generates environments from text prompts or images and lets you explore them as they evolve.
And yes, you can apparently become a seal, a cat, or someone kayaking through an AI-generated world. Walking like a normal human is also an option, although considerably less interesting.

What Odyssey-3 can do:
- Generate interactive 3D-like environments from text prompts
- Use images as starting points for new worlds
- Let you explore in first-person or third-person view
- Move the camera independently
- Introduce new events while the world is being generated
- Predict how objects move and interact using learned physics
But here's where things get interesting.

Odyssey-3 Pro scored 66.1 on Physics-IQ Verified, achieving the highest reported video-to-video benchmark result using best-of-8 sampling.
The benchmark tests how accurately AI models predict the continuation of real physical experiments, covering everything from fluid dynamics to optics and mechanics.
And Odyssey isn't building this technology just for entertainment.

The company is exploring applications in robotics, autonomous vehicles, and AI agents that need to understand and interact with physical environments.
I tried Odyssey-3 Flash in the browser.
The waiting time was around five minutes. Then I got roughly five minutes to explore before being sent back to the queue.
Five minutes to play God. Five minutes to wait. Apparently, even AI-generated universes have capacity limits.
Still, this is a fascinating glimpse of a future where worlds aren't designed in advance. They're generated as you experience them.

Try Odyssey-3:
https://experience.odyssey.systems/
Official announcement:
https://odyssey.systems/meet-odyssey-3

#Odyssey3 #AIWorldModels #GenerativeAI #InteractiveAI #ArtificialIntelligence

items.title: Claude Code Tried to Make Me Watch 60 Videos at Once. I'm Scared.
items.excerpt: I was watching Claude Code coordinate its army of AI agents. And suddenly, things got a little terrifying. The task? Working with 60 videos simultaneously. Claude decided that the most efficient way for me to review the
items.videoDescription:
I was watching Claude Code coordinate its army of AI agents. And suddenly, things got a little terrifying.
The task? Working with 60 videos simultaneously.
Claude decided that the most efficient way for me to review the results was to put all 60 videos on a single screen.

At once.
With everyone talking.
The result? A wall of tiny talking heads, a deafening wall of noise, and one very confused human.
It's hilarious. For now.
But imagine explaining to AI agents in a couple of years why humans can barely handle three tasks at once.

"Oh, I see," the AI will say politely. "Interesting. But why is this biological jelly telling me what to do?"
Welcome to the future of human-AI collaboration.
AI agents are getting faster. Humans aren't.

#ClaudeCode #AIAgents #AgenticAI #Anthropic #FutureOfAI

Someone turned the concept of a web crawler into an actual digital spider.

A glowing, eight-legged creature crawling across text, links, and references on a web page.
It's a creative coding experiment built with JavaScript and CSS, turning something normally invisible into a strangely beautiful digital creature.
Is it useful? Probably not.
Is it mesmerizing? Absolutely.

Sometimes the internet produces something that doesn't need a purpose. It just needs to exist.
This is why I still love the weird side of the internet.
